lesson_title: Two Tariffs, One Graph: Which Is Cheaper?
hook_text: R200 up front for cheaper units — trap or bargain? One crossing point decides.
clip_script: Now the crossing. The two lines meet at exactly one point. Drop from it to the horizontal axis and you land on 250 kilowatt-hours; slide across and you read R625. That is the break-even point: the usage at which both tariffs charge identical money. The break-even matters because it cuts the graph into two decision zones. To the left of 250 units, Option A is cheaper — a light user should not pay R200 for a discount they barely use. To the right, Option B slips below A, because the saving of 80 cents on every unit gradually swallows the fixed fee and keeps going.
visual_style: Two coloured lines racing across a dark graph, the crossing point pulsing, then the two zones flooding green on either side with 'A WINS' and 'B WINS' labels.
pacing: Quick hook, deliberate pause at the crossing, energetic zone reveal.
